mainTopic: Does permitted new growth (גידולי היתר) cancel out the prohibition of the original plant? A proof from a ברייתא about weeding חסיות, and why שביעית is a special case.
overview: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about someone who weeds bulb plants (חסיות) together with a כותי. It then quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling that, once שביעית is over, it is permitted to weed and snack with a Jew suspected of not keeping שביעית. From this, the גמרא tries to prove that גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור, meaning new growth that comes up in a permitted time cancels the prohibition of the original plant. It blocks three ways around the proof: maybe the seed disappears, maybe the plants were crushed, or maybe the case is a mixture. The proof seems to refute רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן, who held that new growth does not cancel the prohibition. רבי יצחק answers that שביעית is different: its prohibition comes through the ground, so the ground can also cancel it. The גמרא challenges this answer with מעשר, which also comes through the ground but is not cancelled by it. It backs up the challenge with a ברייתא about a planted litra of untithed מעשר. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Weeding bulb plants with a Samaritan
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that someone weeding חסיות with a כותי may snack on them, and when he tithes them he treats them as definitely untithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who weeds bulb plants together with a Samaritan may eat a casual snack from them. When he tithes them, he tithes them as produce that is definitely untithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first part of a ברייתא that it will use as a proof. This line sets the scene; the important part for the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכילת עראי (casual snack) does not require tithing, so the weeder may nibble while he works. Since the כותי is assumed not to have tithed, the produce counts as ודאי, definitely untithed, and not just דמאי, doubtfully tithed.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulb vegetables (examples are listed in step 5)
A casual snack, which does not need tithing

phrases.english: One who weeds bulb plants with a Samaritan —
may eat from them a casual snack,
and he tithes them as definitely untithed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weeding חסיות with a כותי: casual snacking is allowed, and tithing is done as ודאי.

steps.title: After שביעית it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rules that if the owner is a Jew suspected about שביעית, weeding with him and eating is permitted once שביעית is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: if the owner is a Jew who is suspected of not keeping the laws of שביעית, then once the שביעית year is over, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling about a Jewish owner suspected about שביעית. This is the line the גמרא will build its proof on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bulbs planted during שביעית by someone who ignores its laws should carry a שביעית prohibition. Yet after שביעית ends, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר permits them. This suggests that the new growth after שביעית removes the original problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected of not keeping the laws of the שמיטה year
The time right after the שמיטה year ends

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
If a Jew is suspected regarding Shemittah,
after the Shemittah year, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means it's permitted to weed with him and snack on the plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שביעית, bulbs belonging to a Jew suspected about שביעית are permitted.

steps.title: Proof that new growth cancels the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that permitted new growth cancels out the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling: new growth that grew after שביעית cancels out the forbidden original bulb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original bulb was forbidden because of שביעית. The only thing that changed is that new, permitted growth came up afterward. So the גמרא suggests the new growth is what made the whole plant permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (introduces an inference)
Growth that came up in a permitted way or time

phrases.english: Is this to say that permitted growths
cancel out the prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּגִידּוּלֵי הֶיתֵּר מַעֲלִין אֶת הָאִיסּוּר
steps.raayaObject: The rule that גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's permission after שביעית

steps.title: Maybe the seed disappears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the case is a plant whose original seed rots away, so nothing forbidden is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is talking about a plant whose seed disappears?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to block the proof by suggesting a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the forbidden seed rots away completely, the plant is permitted simply because the forbidden part is gone. That would prove nothing about new growth cancelling a forbidden part that still exists.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a way to push off a proof)
A plant whose original seed rots away

phrases.english: But perhaps it is about something whose seed disappears?
phrases.notes: In such plants the original forbidden seed rots away, so nothing forbidden is left.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to a plant whose seed disappears
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling may work only because the forbidden part is gone, not because the new growth cancels it.

steps.title: Bulb plants keep their seed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines חסיות as arum, garlic and onions. These are bulbs that do not disappear, so the push-back fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: these are the bulb plants, for example arum, garlic, and onions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the push-back by quoting a ברייתא that lists what חסיות are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arum, garlic and onions are bulbs; the original bulb stays in the ground and does not rot away. So the case cannot be a plant whose seed disappears, and the proof stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But it was taught: these are the bulb plants —
for example, arum, garlic, and onions.

steps.raayaObject: That חסיות are not plants whose seed disappears
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing arum, garlic and onions

steps.title: Maybe the plants were crushed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: maybe the forbidden bulbs were crushed before the new growth sprouted, so the forbidden original was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is talking about crushed plants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way to block the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original bulbs were crushed, the forbidden part would be ruined and gone. Then the permission would again have nothing to do with new growth cancelling a prohibition.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is about crushed ones?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to crushed bulbs
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The forbidden part may have been destroyed, so no cancellation is needed.

steps.title: A suspected person would not bother crushing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of someone suspected about שביעית, and such a person would not take the trouble to crush the plants to avoid the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the crushing idea by pointing to the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing the bulbs would be a careful step to get rid of the שביעית problem. Someone who ignores שביעית would never bother, so the bulbs are whole and the proof stands.

phrases.english: It teaches 'suspected regarding Shemittah.'
phrases.notes: Someone who doesn't care about שביעית wouldn't go to the trouble of crushing the bulbs.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bulbs might have been crushed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person suspected about שביעית would not crush them, so they are whole.

steps.title: Maybe it is a mixture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back a third time: maybe the forbidden bulbs got mixed into a majority of permitted ones and were cancelled that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is talking about a mixture?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more way to block the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a few forbidden bulbs are mixed into many permitted ones, they are cancelled by the majority. That is a different rule from new growth cancelling a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of forbidden and permitted items

phrases.english: But perhaps it is about a mixture?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to a mixture
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The forbidden bulbs might be cancelled by a permitted majority, not by new growth.

steps.title: He eats straight from the ground while weeding
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of someone weeding, who eats the plants right as he pulls them, so there is no chance for a mixture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the mixture idea, again by pointing to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone weeding eats each plant as he pulls it from the ground, before it could be mixed with others. So the case is a single plant, and the proof that new growth cancels the prohibition stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Weeding, pulling up plants from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: All three ways out (seed disappears, crushed, mixture) fail, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר seems to hold that גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור.

phrases.english: It teaches 'one who weeds.'
phrases.notes: He is eating them right as he pulls them up, so they never got mixed with other plants.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bulbs might have been mixed into permitted ones.
steps.terutzMaskana: He eats them while weeding, so no mixture happened.

steps.title: A challenge to רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא shows that new growth cancels the prohibition, it seems to refute רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן, who said it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the proof into a challenge against רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן held that permitted growth does not cancel the prohibition of the original plant, regarding ערלה and כלאי הכרם. The ברייתא seems to say the opposite, so their view looks refuted.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yonatan!
phrases.notes: They said earlier that new growth does not cancel the original prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּדְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן that גידולי היתר אין מעלין את האיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, once all the ways out are blocked, shows new growth does cancel the prohibition.

steps.title: שביעית is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that the שביעית prohibition comes through the ground, so it can also be cancelled through the ground. Other prohibitions are not like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: שביעית is different. Since its prohibition comes through the ground, its cancellation also comes through the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק saves רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן by showing that שביעית is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant becomes forbidden under שביעית because of the ground and the year it grew in. So growing again in the ground after שביעית can also undo the prohibition. That logic does not carry over to ערלה or כלאים, so רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן's rule still holds there.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יצחק, the ברייתא shows that new growth cancels a prohibition only for שביעית, whose prohibition comes from the ground. That would leave the general view of רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן intact, but the next step challenges this distinction.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק does not say new growth cancels prohibitions in general. He limits it to שביעית, so this is an exception and not a change to the general rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that what the ground forbids the ground can undo, is what protects רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן. The very next step tests it against מעשר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Shemittah is different,
since its prohibition comes through the ground —
its cancellation also comes through the ground.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שביעית is a special exception)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves new growth always cancels the prohibition, which would refute רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שביעית, whose prohibition comes from the ground, is cancelled by regrowth in the ground.

steps.title: What about tithes? They come from the ground but are not cancelled by it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's rule. מעשר is also a prohibition that comes through the ground, yet the ground does not cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at מעשר: its prohibition comes through the ground, and still the ground does not cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יצחק's answer from Step 11 by bringing a counter-example, מעשר. This step makes the claim, and the next step brings the source that backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's rule was: if a prohibition comes through the ground, the ground can also cancel it. מעשר fits the first half, because produce only owes tithes because it grew from the ground. If the ground does not cancel מעשר, then רבי יצחק's rule is not a general principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe, a portion of produce that must be separated
But look at / here is (introduces a counter-example)

phrases.english: But there is the case of tithe,
whose prohibition comes through the ground,
yet its cancellation does not come through the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, דְּאִיסּוּרוֹ עַל יְדֵי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle רבי יצחק gave in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that whatever is forbidden through the ground can be cancelled through the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: מעשר is forbidden through the ground but is not cancelled through the ground, so the rule fails.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a planted litra of untithed tithe
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that when untithed מעשר is planted and grows tenfold, the original amount still owes its tithe. The person must separate it from other produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if someone planted a litra of מעשר that was still טבל, and it grew to about ten litras, the new growth owes מעשר and is subject to שביעית. For the original litra, he must separate what it owed from produce somewhere else, according to the calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the claim from Step 12. It shows that planting untithed מעשר did not wipe out its obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the new growth had cancelled the original litra, nothing more would be owed for it. Instead, the ברייתא requires him to pay what that litra owed, using other produce. So the ground did not cancel the מעשר prohibition, and this contradicts רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: A litra, a measure of weight
Produce whose required portions have not yet been separated

steps.whatToRemember: With מעשר, planting does not cancel the original obligation. The original litra must still be tithed for from elsewhere. This challenges רבי יצחק's claim that the ground cancels what the ground forbids.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next move. The גמרא must now explain why שביעית is different from מעשר, or else רבי יצחק's answer to רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן falls apart.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A litra of untithed tithe
phrases.notes: This is מעשר ראשון that still has not had its own tithe, תרומת מעשר, taken off.

phrases.english: which one sowed in the ground
and it grew,
and it is now about ten litras,
it is obligated in tithe and in the laws of the seventh year.
And that original litra,
he tithes for it from a different place
according to the calculation!
phrases.notes: He works out how much that one litra owed and separates that amount from other produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לִיטְרָא מַעֲשֵׂר טֶבֶל שֶׁזְּרָעָהּ בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that proves the counter-example raised in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר is not cancelled by new growth from the ground.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a litra of untithed מעשר that was planted and grew to ten litras, where the original litra must still be tithed for from elsewhere.
